messages.subject: Re: Naturalist Italian student
parts:
Dear Ms. Iossa:

I have been doing line transects surveys of forest ungulates in India
for about 14 years and have used DISTANCE and its predecessors TRANSECT
and SIZETRAN. The following references may be useful:

Karanth K. U. 1991. Line transect method for censusing elephants in
Nagarahole. Pages 51-52 in Censusing elephants in forests (Editors: U.
Ramakrishnan, J. A. Santhosh and R. Sukumar). Asian Elephant
Conservation Centre, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore, India.


Karanth K. U. and Sunquist M. E. 1992. Population structure, density
and biomass of large herbivores in the tropical forests of Nagarahole,
India. Journal of Tropical Ecology 8: 21-35.

Karanth K. U. and Sunquist M. E. 1995. Prey selection by tiger,
leopard and dhole in tropical forests. Journal of Animal Ecology 64:
439-450.

Karanth K. U. and Nichols J. D. 1998. Estimating tiger densities in
India from camera trap data using photographic captures and recaptures.
Ecology Vol 79 (8): 2852-2862.

Karanth K. U. Estimation of large mammal densities using line transect
sampling: a case study from Nagarahole National Park. In Proceedings of
the Workshop on Field Research Methods. Eds. A. J. T. Johnsingh, S. P.
Goyal, P. K. Mathur, S. Choudhury and P. Krausman. Wildlife Institute of
India, Dehra Dun, India (In Press).

Karanth K. U. and Stith B. M. 1999. Prey depletion as a critical
determinant of tiger population viability. In Riding the Tiger: Tiger
conservation in human dominated landscapes (Editors: J. Seidensticker,
S. Christie and P. Jackson), Cambridge University Press.

I hope you will find some of these useful. All the best,
KARANTH
